text.p: Grossman's Inc said Tuesday it had completed a deal with Jeld-Wen Inc that provides the money necessary for Grossman's to stay in business.
In January Grossman's announced it had run out of money and might file for Chapter 11 protection under the Bankruptcy Code.

Between then and now the company structured a deal in which Jeld-Wen has loaned Grossman's $3.1 million, has backed an increase in Grossman's line of credit, and has taken three of Grossman's seven board seats.
But Grossman's said today it was still going to file for Chapter 11 protection in the near future.
It said Seymour Kroll has succeeded David Ferrari as interim president and chief executive.
Robert Swanson, who stepped down as chief executive in February, continues as chairman, it said.
Chief Financial Officer Michael Shea resigned Monday and no successor has been named, the company said.
Grossman's said the size of its board has been reduced from eight members to seven, and four members of the previous board have resigned -- John Grey, Maurice Grossman, Leo Kahn and Samuel Witt III.
Three top Jeld-Wen officers -- Richard Wendt, Theodore Schnormeier and Larry Wetter -- have been elected to the board, the company said.
Grossman's said it, Jeld-Wen and Congress Financial Corp agreed to basic terms and are working to finalize an arrangement that would increase the credit provided by Congress.
Under present plans, Grossman's said an increase in the credit line will be supported by a stand-by letter of credit put in place by an affiliate of Jeld-Wen in favor of Congress.

Congress recently notified Grossman's that it was in default of its credit line due to adverse business conditions. Congress has not yet exercised any of its remedies available upon default and has informed the company that in conjunction with the letter of credit agreement with Jeld-Wen, it will currently forbear all known defaults, Grossman's said.
